context_engagements.note: Recorded without a connection line. He is named only as the preferred companion; nothing states what passed between him and Boulton.

sources.quote: Will you come and see me tonight at nine o'clock or any time when you can escape from 'Sir John' - whom by the bye I believe you like much better than yours truly
sources.context: Wilde to Harold Boulton, [? April 1878], Magdalen College (MS Yale). 'much better' is italicised in the printed text. The editors identify 'Sir John' as most probably Sir John Alexander Hanham, ninth Baronet, Magdalen undergraduate 1875-8. He is the rival in the only letter that carries `boulton--wilde`.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: That Boulton had a preferred companion, and who the editors think he was.
sources.provenance: Repo PDF page 93; printed folio 66 confirmed on the rendered page image, read 2026-08-05.

name: Sir John Alexander Hanham
bio: Ninth Baronet, and a Magdalen undergraduate from 1875 to 1878, having succeeded to the baronetcy on his uncle's death in 1877. He is on this map as the third point of a triangle: the 'Sir John' whose company Wilde believed Harold Boulton preferred to his own.
bio_note: Added 2026-08-06. NO CONNECTION LINE OF HIS OWN - nothing records what he felt about anyone, and he appears in the record only as the man Wilde was jealous of. HE IS LOAD-BEARING ANYWAY: `boulton--wilde` is an attraction-expressed edge drawn entirely on Wilde's pique that Boulton liked someone 'much better than yours truly', and leaving that someone unnamed left the edge's evidence half-invisible. IDENTIFICATION IS THE EDITORS' AND IS HEDGED - 'most probably Sir John Alexander Hanham' (printed 66, note 2) - and that hedge is kept rather than dropped. See [[boulton]].
